in_hebrew.name: סביון
in_hebrew.meaning: שם פרטי נדיר עם משמעות לא ברורה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סביון הוא שם פרטי נדיר שמקורו לא ברור. אין לו אזכור ישיר בתנך או בספרות היהודית הקדומה. ייתכן כי השם קשור למילה 'סב', שפירושה 'זקן' או 'אב'. השימוש בשם זה עשוי להיות קשור למסורות נוצריות ולא יהודיות.

in_greek.name: Σεβίων
in_greek.meaning: Όνομα με πιθανή σύνδεση στη λατινική λέξη 'sebios', σεβαστός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σεβίων πιθανόν να συνδέεται με τη λατινική λέξη 'sebios' ή 'σεβαστός', που σημαίνει 'εὐσεβής' ή 'σεβασμός'. Η χρήση αυτού του ονόματος μπορεί να σχετίζεται με την πρώιμη Εκκλησία και την επίδραση της λατινικής γλώσσας στη ονοματολογία της εποχής.

historical_references.reference: Sebion of Byzantium, a fourth-century Christian theologian and bishop, who wrote extensively on the Trinity and the nature of Christ. He was a member of the so-called 'Anomoean party' that disputed the divinity of the Holy Spirit relative to the Father and the Son. Sebion is also known for his opposition to the 'Sabellian' doctrine, which held that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were successive modes or expressions of a single divine substance rather than distinct persons.
historical_references.time_period: Late Roman Empire, Fourth Century AD
historical_references.context: Theological debates and controversies surrounding the nature of the Holy Trinity and the persons of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

historical_references.reference: Sebion of Carthage, a bishop in North Africa during the Vandal period, who is known for his opposition to the Arian heresy that denied the full divinity of Christ. He was a strong proponent of the Catholic doctrine of the Trinity and wrote several treatises defending this doctrine against Arian and Semi-Arian opponents. Sebion was one of the bishops who attended the Council of Carthage in 411 AD, which was called to address the Arian controversy.
historical_references.context: Theological debates and controversies surrounding the nature of Christ and the doctrine of the Trinity.
